articles.title: Residential Steel Framing: A Guide for General Contractors
articles.audience: General contractors and custom-home builders
articles.purpose: Decide whether adding project-specific residential steel framing is a suitable option for the GC’s work.
articles.practicalOutput: A concise adoption overview and project-fit summary describing Wheeler supply, builder-crew assembly, crew preparation and design-team involvement.
articles.scope: Residential project fit; substantiated material advantages; Wheeler’s supply and on-site assembly model; overview of responsibilities and the adoption sequence.

articles.title: How to Compare Custom-Home Steel Framing Quotes in Southern California
articles.audience: Homeowners and builders comparing proposals
articles.purpose: Normalize two or more actual framing proposals for the same approved home design.
articles.practicalOutput: A side-by-side worksheet with rows for engineering/coordination, supply/preparation, transport, installation, wall-performance scope, quoted amount, excluded work and comparable adjusted total.
articles.scope: Record the same design and estimate date; align included scope and responsibilities; enter separately quoted missing work; compare equivalent totals; identify unresolved financial inputs.

articles.title: Wood to Cold-Formed Steel Framing: Preparing Your Crew
articles.audience: GCs and framing crews transitioning from wood
articles.purpose: Prepare a wood-framing crew to understand the material-specific knowledge required for cold-formed steel.
articles.practicalOutput: A learning matrix: transferable skill, material-specific difference, preparation or education needed, and the responsible source of approved project information.
articles.scope: Plan reading and layout skills; specified-system equipment and handling awareness; structural framing versus partitions; current industry education; limits of crew decisions and communication with the design team.

articles.title: Steel vs. Wood Framing Costs: Comparing the Installed Budget
articles.audience: Owners and builders comparing framing materials
articles.purpose: Compare the initial installed framing budget for equivalent engineered wood and steel designs.
articles.practicalOutput: A phase-by-phase cost-category table showing the design basis, quantity/scope, responsible party and project-specific estimate required for each alternative.
articles.scope: Complete structural scope including required heavy steel; design and preparation labor; crew installation; deliveries and waste allowances; finish preparation and equivalent exterior-wall energy performance.

articles.title: Custom Steel Framing vs. Panelized and Modular Homes in Los Angeles
articles.audience: Custom-home owners, architects and builders evaluating delivery models
articles.purpose: Explain the differences between material, off-site preparation and whole-home delivery methods.
articles.practicalOutput: A delivery-method comparison matrix distinguishing framing material, off-site preparation, preassembled panels and volumetric modules; compare customization, scope and logistics without treating these categories as mutually exclusive.
articles.scope: Definitions and overlaps; customization and repetition; supplier scope; factory quality checks; total schedule and logistics; Wheeler’s custom supply and complementary panelized work.

articles.title: Steel vs. Wood Framing for a Wildfire Rebuild
articles.audience: Southern California homeowners rebuilding after wildfire
articles.purpose: Explain the material and planning factors that shape a rebuild framing decision.
articles.practicalOutput: A homeowner material-decision worksheet comparing noncombustibility, material behavior, crew readiness, engineered scope and budget inputs for the actual rebuild.
articles.scope: Combustibility and moisture behavior; complete-home resilience; project budget and crew readiness; approved design and framing scope; connection to existing local rebuild pages.

articles.title: First Residential Steel-Framing Job: A Site-Readiness Checklist
articles.audience: GCs planning their first residential steel job
articles.purpose: Confirm the actual project is ready for framing delivery and crew assembly.
articles.practicalOutput: An ordered readiness checklist with responsible party and completion evidence for approved drawings, installation lead, unloading, staging, handling, shared trade access and escalation arrangements.
articles.scope: Confirm installation responsibility and current approved information; arrange delivery and site access; organize staging and protection; coordinate trade routes and communication; route design changes through the responsible professionals.

articles.title: Custom-Home Steel Framing: Design Inputs and Team Responsibilities
articles.audience: Architects, engineers and custom-home builders
articles.purpose: Provide a design-stage input and responsibility matrix.
articles.practicalOutput: A design-input and responsibility matrix covering architectural geometry, structural/specialty engineering, service information and current approved drawings.
articles.scope: Architectural inputs; structural and specialty engineering roles; service coordination; revision and approval sequence; early CFS familiarity before procurement.

articles.title: California Wildfire Insurance Discounts: Programs and Calculations
articles.audience: Homeowners budgeting wildfire insurance
articles.purpose: Understand published California wildfire discount opportunities and calculate the premium component to which they apply.
articles.practicalOutput: A sourced program comparison table and the existing labeled $6,000/$2,000/30% arithmetic example showing a $600 reduction.
articles.scope: Mercury mitigation and designation ranges; construction-classification conditions; FAIR Plan schedule; premium component and nonadditive tiers; insurer-specific underwriting.

articles.title: Steel Framing and Wildfire Resilience: A Rebuild Planning Checklist
articles.audience: Homeowners rebuilding in wildfire-exposed communities
articles.purpose: Record the whole-home resilience decisions and evidence a homeowner’s rebuild team must coordinate alongside the steel framing.
articles.practicalOutput: A rebuild planning checklist with rows for roof, exterior-wall covering, openings, vents, property surroundings and maintenance; identify the decision, responsible role and project-specific evidence without supplying assembly recipes.
articles.scope: Briefly define the contribution of noncombustible framing; organize whole-home design and maintenance decisions in a usable checklist; record applicable design/evidence and professional responsibility; connect to existing Wheeler fire-resilience and local rebuild pages.

articles.title: Steel Framing for Open-Plan Homes: Layout and Trade Coordination
articles.audience: Architects and builders designing open-plan homes
articles.purpose: Explain how architectural openness and the engineered framing are coordinated.
articles.practicalOutput: An open-plan design-input table for room volumes, large openings, service routes, finish interfaces and architectural/engineering coordination.
articles.scope: Room volumes and openings; project-specific structural evaluation; service routes and soffits; finish interfaces; early supplier and engineering coordination.

articles.title: Selecting a Steel Framing Supplier for a Los Angeles Custom Home
articles.audience: Custom-home owners and builders preparing a supplier shortlist
articles.purpose: Provide a supplier-fit comparison matrix tied to an actual residential design.
articles.practicalOutput: A supplier-fit matrix for the approved residential design: actual supplied scope, customization, project experience, design-team interface, lead-time phases and local delivery requirements.
articles.scope: Design range and actual supplied scope; approval responsibilities; logistics and complete lead time; production and installation checks; relevant project experience and product documents.

articles.title: Steel Framing, Fire-Rated Assemblies and Type II Construction
articles.audience: Architects, engineers and builders evaluating fire performance
articles.purpose: Clearly distinguish the three performance and classification concepts.
articles.practicalOutput: A clear three-concept comparison: noncombustible material, the tested/approved complete assembly and whole-building Type II classification, with the scope and responsible evaluator for each.
articles.scope: Material combustibility; complete assembly ratings; construction classification; steel with combustible adjacent products; professional approval; evidence scope.

articles.title: Builders’ Risk Insurance for Steel-Framed Homes: Coverage Basics
articles.audience: Homeowners and GCs arranging construction-period insurance
articles.purpose: Explain the insurance stage and covered-property categories relevant during construction.
articles.practicalOutput: A construction-stage coverage table explaining the structure, project materials, locations/timing and policy-dependent covered-loss categories, followed by a clear transition to completed-home insurance.
articles.scope: Structure and materials; on-site and transit cover; installed or awaiting-installation equipment; covered causes and project duration; policy-specific scope; distinction from completed-home insurance.

articles.title: Wood vs. Steel Framing: A Long-Term Cost Worksheet
articles.audience: Owners evaluating costs after occupancy
articles.purpose: Build a transparent post-occupancy cost comparison using the owner’s estimates and dated property-specific quotations.
articles.practicalOutput: A worksheet separating one-time installed cost from annual insurance, expected maintenance, finish-repair allowances and any periodic replacement costs; record the source/date, time horizon and assumption for each input.
articles.scope: Separate initial and recurring expenses; establish a stated comparison period; enter actual quotations or clearly labeled assumptions; calculate the sum consistently; show how changing a recurring input changes the result; review which assumptions require updating.

articles.title: IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home: Requirements and Designation
articles.audience: Rebuilding homeowners pursuing a property designation
articles.purpose: Plan and complete the whole-property measures needed for an IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home designation.
articles.practicalOutput: An Essential/Enhanced scope comparison and a chronological designation roadmap covering completed-property application, required evidence, evaluation, certificate duration and ongoing reviews.
articles.scope: Essential and Enhanced protection scope; whole-home exterior and immediate surroundings; coordination during rebuild design; completed-property application and evidence; evaluation, designation duration and maintenance.

articles.title: Steel Framing for Complex Roofs: A Design Coordination Guide
articles.audience: Architects and builders designing complex residential roofs
articles.purpose: Explain the information flow for a custom roof design without component fabrication instructions.
articles.practicalOutput: A roof-design coordination brief covering overall geometry, intended room volumes, service/finish interfaces and the approved-information review sequence.
articles.scope: Geometry and room volumes; architectural and engineering requirements; service and finish interfaces; approved overall residential examples; review before production.

articles.title: Wildfire Rebuild Team: Design, Construction and Framing Roles
articles.audience: Homeowners assembling a rebuild team
articles.purpose: Explain which party leads each design, supply and construction responsibility.
articles.practicalOutput: A homeowner-facing role-and-handoff table distinguishing the architect, structural engineer, builder, framing supplier and installing crew across rebuild stages.
articles.scope: Architectural design; structural engineering; GC construction management; framing supply and crew assembly; shared information and approvals; framing within the whole-home resilience plan.

articles.title: Wood vs. Steel Framing: Material Stability and Finish Coordination
articles.audience: General contractors and custom-home builders coordinating material selection and finished surfaces
articles.purpose: Understand how the chosen framing material affects dimensional consistency and coordination of finished surfaces.
articles.practicalOutput: A material-behavior comparison and a finish-interface checklist for coordination with the design team and finishing trades.
articles.scope: Wood moisture response and actual wood-product differences; manufactured steel dimensional consistency and temperature movement; plane alignment for drywall, cabinetry, tile and exterior finishes; rot, termites and corrosion protection; complete-building workmanship and exposure.

articles.title: Steel Framing Proposal Terms: Allowances, Exclusions and Revisions
articles.audience: Builders and owners evaluating financial proposal terms
articles.purpose: Understand how the stated commercial terms of one framing proposal determine the price boundary and later adjustments.
articles.practicalOutput: A term/effect table and clearly labeled generic scenarios for an allowance adjustment, separately quoted excluded work and a separately priced design revision.
articles.scope: Included base scope; allowance versus confirmed price; excluded work and the party arranging it; quantities and estimate date; separately priced revisions and replacement work; record of agreed financial responsibility.

articles.title: Fire and Code Documentation for Steel-Framed Homes
articles.audience: Architects and builders organizing project evidence
articles.purpose: Provide a document-purpose and responsibility matrix distinct from the fire terminology explainer.
articles.practicalOutput: A professional document-purpose matrix mapping product submittals, manufacturer certifications, assembly-specific evidence and approved project classification information to their provider and reviewer.
articles.scope: Manufacturer certification and product submittals; assembly-specific test or approval evidence; approved project design and classification; structural engineer and code-team review; scope of each document.

articles.title: Steel Framing for Hillside Homes: Access and Delivery Planning
articles.audience: Architects and builders planning constrained hillside residential sites
articles.purpose: Explain how access and site logistics connect to framing planning.
articles.practicalOutput: A constrained-site access and delivery planning record identifying approach/unloading constraints, staging space, shared trade use and approved coordination information.
articles.scope: Truck access and unloading; staging and handling; constrained working space; shared trade use; custom architectural inputs and approved information. Keep the entire article outside foundation and anchoring work.

articles.title: Curved Steel Framing: Preparing a Custom-Home Design Brief
articles.audience: Architects developing unusual residential geometry
articles.purpose: Explain the architectural information needed to evaluate nonstandard forms.
articles.practicalOutput: An architectural design brief recording intended curves, overall nonstandard geometry, finish alignment, relevant drawings and project-specific professional evaluation.
articles.scope: Curves, stairs, tall spaces and vaults at overall design level; intended geometry and finish alignment; approved drawing coordination; project-specific engineering. No bendable-track methods or fabrication demonstrations.

articles.title: Comparing Insurance Quotes for a Wood- or Steel-Framed Home
articles.audience: Homeowners comparing property-specific insurance costs
articles.purpose: Compare actual completed-home insurance quotations for the same property with different approved construction descriptions.
articles.practicalOutput: A policy-comparison worksheet matching property, reconstruction-value basis, coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions, period, mitigation evidence and total quoted premium.
articles.scope: Record the construction description accepted by each insurer; hold coverage and deductible assumptions consistent; distinguish total premium from any wildfire component; reconcile terms and remaining coverage differences; record quote dates and continuing conditions.

articles.title: Steel-Framed Exterior Walls: Fire, Moisture and Thermal Performance
articles.audience: Architects and builders coordinating the building envelope
articles.purpose: Explain the complete exterior-wall performance interfaces at a general design level.
articles.practicalOutput: A general exterior-wall coordination matrix connecting fire-exposure goals, moisture protection, thermal bridging/control and finish interfaces to the complete-wall design and responsible professional.
articles.scope: Steel conduction and continuous insulation; wall versus material performance; exterior fire exposure and openings; moisture protection and finishes; coordinated design responsibilities. No component dimensions or assembly recipes.

articles.title: Custom Steel Framing in Panelized Homes: Scope and Coordination
articles.audience: GCs coordinating custom requirements alongside panelized work
articles.purpose: Explain the roles and information needed when custom framing complements a panelized approach.
articles.practicalOutput: A scope-and-information coordination matrix for custom steel framing supplied alongside a panelized approach: assigned supply scope, shared approved drawings, design responsibility and delivery/trade interfaces.
articles.scope: Define each supplied scope; retain overall architect and engineer responsibility; align approved drawings and production information; coordinate delivery and remaining trades; provider-specific terms. Do not invent a completed hybrid case or describe proprietary connections.

articles.title: Wheeler’s Reported Steel Framing Savings: Three Project Comparisons
articles.audience: Owners and builders assessing reported cost examples
articles.purpose: Interpret Wheeler’s three reported residential dollar-savings examples by keeping each project and comparison baseline separate.
articles.practicalOutput: A three-row evidence table: reported project size/budget, compared framing alternatives, saving as reported, scope to which it applies and what the example establishes.
articles.scope: More than $200,000 on a $2 million project; at least $160,000 of heavy structural steel on a 10,000-square-foot wood/CFS comparison; $250,000 of heavy structural steel on a 5,000-square-foot site-assembled/panelized comparison; preserve separate baselines and attribution.

articles.title: Steel Framing Waste and Deliveries: A Contractor’s Tracking Guide
articles.audience: General contractors managing residential framing deliveries, site waste and hauling
articles.purpose: Track framing resource use during the job so delivery, waste and cleanup performance can be evaluated consistently.
articles.practicalOutput: A reusable tracking table with design/scope basis, material deliveries, waste-hauling trips, measured site-waste volume, cleanup/haulage costs, measurement period and comparison method.
articles.scope: Separate framing deliveries from waste hauling; record site waste separately from off-site waste; retain project size and scope; use Wheeler’s attributed truck-trip/waste examples to explain metrics; identify how logs support future planning.

articles.title: Steel Framing Credentials: Product and Contractor Verification
articles.audience: Homeowners evaluating evidence supplied by project participants
articles.purpose: Explain what each credential establishes and how to verify the relevant party.
articles.practicalOutput: A homeowner verification table identifying manufacturer product certificates, relevant contractor licensing, industry membership and property designations; distinguish the subject, verification source and limits of each.
articles.scope: Manufacturer product certification and matching submittals; contractor verification through CSLB; CFSEI membership versus certification; ASTM material testing; assembly/classification versus property designation. Do not assert Wheeler holds a contractor license or IBHS designation.
